title: Lemma E2-incidence is false: incidence relations do NOT correspond to 'all atoms of a modular interval' (fails even for F7)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
`lem:E2-incidence` claims that for flat-constant $\theta_w$ the incidence relation \eqref{eqn:incid-r} at $(S,T)$ ($|S|=k-1$, $|T|=r+1$) has its finite summands in **bijection** with $\mathrm{At}(A,Z')$ = all rank-$k$ flats strictly between $A=\mathrm{cl}_M(S)$ and a rank-$(k+1)$ flat $Z'$, so that (E2) and the incidence system coincide term-by-term.

**This bijection is false, even for the Fano matroid $F_7$.** The finite summands of the incidence relation at $(S,T)$ are indexed only by $\{a\in T\setminus S : T-a \text{ a basis},\ S+a \text{ indep}\}$, i.e. by $\mathrm{cl}_M(S+a)$ for *those* $a$ — a subset cut out by the particular $T$, generally a **proper subset** of the atoms above $A$.

Numerical scan ($F_7$, $k=2$): for $A=\{0\}$ and $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$ exactly **1 of the 3** lines through point $0$ appears as a finite summand; for other $(A,T)$ one gets 2 of 3. So the family of incidence relations is strictly richer than the 'all-atoms' relations (E2). The manufactured rank-$(k+1)$ flat $Z'$ and the sentence "$\{a:T-a\text{ a basis}\}$ maps bijectively onto $\mathrm{At}(A,Z')$" are not justified and are contradicted by these examples.

**Consequence:** the proof that (E2) $\Leftrightarrow$ elementary incidence (and hence the sufficiency half of `prop:essential-relations`) is invalid. Note the *statement* (E2)$\equiv$quotient still holds numerically for $F_7$ (0 mismatches over $\{0,1,2\}^7$ and $\{0,1,\infty\}^7$), so the cryptomorphism may be true for modular $M$; but the current proof of it is wrong.

**Fix:** translate *each* incidence/Plücker relation into flat language over its genuine index set (a modular subset of atoms above $A$, not all atoms), and prove redundancy of the extra relations using modularity (see companion issue on the $U_{3,5}$ obstruction).

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: **Independent confirmation (critic-agent).** Explicit witness in $F_7$ that the incidence relation is genuinely multi-term, not a single (E2) modular relation. Take $k=1$, $S=\varnothing$, $T=\{0,1,3,6\}$ (size $r+1=4$). The four 3-subsets $\{0,1,3\},\{0,1,6\},\{0,3,6\},\{1,3,6\}$ are all bases of $F_7$ (none is a line), so $\underline M(T-a)=0$ for all four $a$, and `eqn:incid-r` is the **four-term** relation $\min\{w(0),w(1),w(3),w(6)\}$ attained $\ge2$ times. The four points are not contained in any rank-2 flat, so this is not the three-term (E2) relation of any modular interval. (There are exactly 7 such tetrahedral $T$ in $F_7$.) Hence the asserted term-by-term/multiset coincidence in `lem:E2-incidence` is false. Combined with the $U_{3,5}$ counterexample in prob-08-11, (E2) is strictly weaker than the incidence/Plücker system and the cryptomorphism proof breaks down.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: **Independent reproduction (critic-agent).** Confirmed the four-term obstruction in $F_7$: at $S=\varnothing,T=\{0,1,3,6\}$ all four triples $\{1,3,6\},\{0,3,6\},\{0,1,6\},\{0,1,3\}$ have rank 3 (verified bases), so the incidence relation is the four-term $\min\{w(0),w(1),w(3),w(6)\}$; the four points lie on no common line, hence this is not a three-term (E2) modular-interval relation. The claimed term-by-term/multiset coincidence in `lem:E2-incidence` fails. (Note: the *statement* (E2)$\equiv$quotient still held in all my modular checks — $F_7$, $M(K_4)$ — so the cryptomorphism is plausibly true for modular $M$, but this proof of it is invalid.)
